mid_card_failures_disclosed: Draft files landed outside the card's write_scope (client_events.go, protocol_schema.go); renamed to the registered client_protocol*.go pattern before any evidence was recorded.
First fixture-grading pass used a hand-written JSON Schema subset; replaced by the repository's existing jsonschema/v6 compiler (the same path LoadContracts uses) so no second validator survives.

Real defects found by the qualification and fixed in code, not by weakening the check: (1) the event journal inserted its outbox row before the watermark CAS, so a failed CAS left an orphan event when the caller committed - now wrapped in a SAVEPOINT that rolls the pair back together; (2) event ids derived from command_id collided across principals replaying the same text - now keyed by (session, sequence); (3) a takeover advanced writer_epoch but not writer_client_id, so the new writer was locked out - the attribution now moves in the same transaction; (4) SQLite applies each json_extract path independently, so nested payload lookups silently returned NULL - switched to single dotted paths; (5) session.attach with request_write_owner was routed to the read handler, so a takeover never passed the writer gate; (6) ACKNOWLEDGED answers were not schema-shaped (they need PendingResult) and ControlResult needs a typed snapshot - handlers now emit contract-shaped results and every own output is validated before it is stored; (7) a checker bug printed PASS with zero recorded assertions - the reporter now fails closed on panic and on an empty assertion list.

The published RelativePath pattern uses negative lookaheads that Go's RE2 (and therefore the repo's schema compiler, which validates patterns against the metaschema) cannot compile. The loader accepts only that exact published text, replaces it with an accept-all pattern, and re-enforces its documented semantics (non-empty, no NUL, not absolute, no drive prefix, no '..' segment) both when the definition itself and when any property declared as RelativePath is validated. Any other un-compilable pattern makes loading fail closed, and the assertion CONTRACT-NEUTRALISED-PATTERNS-EXACTLY-1 pins the count at 1.

W03-02-OUTPUT.evidence: CLI and Desktop use one typed service: the same domain.ClientService instance answers both direct calls and POST /v2/command behind api.Handler; the qualification asserts equality of the typed result, the journaled watermark and the revision over the HTTP path (HTTP-HOST-STATUS-TYPED, HTTP-CANCEL-ACKNOWLEDGED, HTTP-CANCEL-JOURNALED-ONCE, HTTP-REPLAY-NO-SECOND-EFFECT). All 106 published fixtures replay exactly (76 accepted / 30 rejected) against the pinned schema plus the runtime decoders, and request, response and event paths each have positive and negative cases (136 assertions).

W03-02-NEGATIVE.evidence: Bare-object success, cross-method results, old-protocol downgrade, swallowed error payloads and duplicate side effects are all refused: BARE-OBJECT-REJECT, BARE-RESULT-SCHEMA-REJECT, CROSS-METHOD-RESULT-REJECT, OLD-PROTOCOL-NO-DOWNGRADE, HTTP-OLD-PROTOCOL-BEFORE-AUTH, NON-REJECT-WITH-ERROR-REJECT, REJECT-WITHOUT-ERROR-OBJECT, ACK-CLAIMS-SETTLEMENT-REJECT, REPLAY-ZERO-SECOND-EFFECT, CONFLICT-SAME-KEY-DIFFERENT-REQUEST, CONFLICT-NO-STATE-DRIFT, APPEND-REUSE-REJECT, APPEND-HOLE-REJECT, APPEND-DUPLICATE-EVENT-ID-REJECT, FAILED-COMMAND-NO-ORPHAN-EVENT, JOURNAL-DELETE-BLOCKED, JOURNAL-UPDATE-BLOCKED, CREDENTIAL-IN-RESPONSE-REJECTED, SENSITIVE-EVENT-REJECTED, RELPATH-REJECT-* (12 cases).

negative_cases: command_id replay returns the stored answer and writes neither a second event nor a second revision
same command_id with a different request body -> ErrIdemConflict, transaction rolled back, no drift
a different principal is graded in its own idempotency namespace, never served another user's stored reply
takeover with a stale expected_revision answers VERSION_CONFLICT carrying the live revision
takeover by the current writer client is WRITER_BUSY and moves no epoch or revision
a takeover that claims writer_epoch is refused at the decode boundary and changes nothing
two concurrent takeovers on one session: exactly one ACKNOWLEDGED, the other VERSION_CONFLICT, epoch +1
after a transfer the old epoch is STALE_WRITER_EPOCH and the new writer's write succeeds
cancel is only reported settled when the run row itself records a confirmed cancel with teardown flags
cancel on a terminal run without confirmation is ALREADY_TERMINAL; on a foreign run NOT_FOUND
PAUSE/RESUME are NOT_IMPLEMENTED rejections instead of fake settlements
event sequence reuse, holes, stale epoch, stale revision, a stream without START and a duplicate event id are each refused with their own error
forged journal rows are detectable as gaps; DELETE/UPDATE on outbox are blocked by the durable triggers
credential material is legal only in the native import request direction and is rejected in any response, event or snapshot
cross-project session and run references never resolve and never leak the real owner
sealed sessions reject writes and event appends (SESSION_ARCHIVED / ErrSealed)
known_limitations_and_obligations: Writer attribution is still the envelope's client_id, checked against the session row; binding the writer to the authenticated OS principal (22 §OS bootstrap) belongs to the handoff/native-bootstrap card. Recorded as a new carry-forward obligation, not silently closed.

host.status reports config_revision 0 and a snapshot emits schema-legal nulls for checkpoint_artifact_ref, transcript_artifact_ref, pending_command_ids and pending_permissions; the subsystems that fill them are later cards, so no value is invented here.

The writer lease TTL comes from RESEARCHOS_WRITER_LEASE_TTL (default 15m, mirroring the existing credential TTL ceiling); a handoff is refused if the policy is missing rather than publishing a fabricated lease.
internal/api embeds byte-identical copies of the two pinned schemas and verifies their sha256 at startup; a mismatch closes /v2/command with HOST_UNAVAILABLE instead of downgrading.
protocol.v2_roundtrip stays UNBOUND: it points at a python test that does not exist yet and is not this card's binding line.
apps/cli and apps/desktop were not modified by this card (outside write_scope); they keep using the same host, and their v2 client wiring belongs to their own cards.
